---
title: "Ask Rill and Orientation"
---

Rill has two optional agent features. Ask Rill answers questions about the
story you are reading. Orientation suggests what to read next. Both work from
Rill's stored copies of articles and keep the article's own words apart from
the agent's commentary.

Both use the model named by `RILL_AGENT_MODEL`, through
[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org) and a
[deputy](https://github.com/JamesHWade/deputy) agent. The agent can read only
what Rill hands it. It cannot browse the web, read or write files, run shell
commands, or run R code.

## Ask Rill

Open a story and choose **Ask Rill**. The panel beside the story sends your
question and the story's stored copy to the provider, and the footer names
where it goes. The agent reads the copy through a single read-only tool. Its
answers quote the story for claims the text supports, label interpretation,
and say when the story doesn't answer the question.

Each question runs with fixed limits: at most 8 model requests, 16 tool calls,
128,000 tokens, US$2 of estimated cost, and five minutes. You can stop a
response while it streams and retry one that failed.

The chat panel shows the conversation for the current browser session. Rill
also keeps a record of each question: the question, the answer, which copy of
the story it used, and how it ended. **Reopen last answer** in the sidebar
brings back your latest answer with the copy it was based on. In the demo,
these records last until R restarts.

## Orientation

With no story open, Rill shows Orientation: up to three unread stories worth
reading now, each with a short explanation and the passage it is based on.
**Not for me** removes a pick. The rest of the unread queue is grouped into up
to five topics, and each topic opens a filtered queue. Opening a pick does not
mark it as endorsed.

Orientation is off by default because it sends article text to the provider
without you asking a question. To make it available:

```text
RILL_AGENT_MODEL=openai
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key
RILL_ORIENTATION_ENABLED=true
RILL_AGENT_POLICY_URL=https://openai.com/policies/row-privacy-policy/
```

Each Reader then turns it on from the sidebar. The confirmation names the
provider and endpoint and links to the policy in `RILL_AGENT_POLICY_URL`.
Rill remembers the confirmation for that exact endpoint. Changing the endpoint
turns Orientation off until the Reader confirms again. Upgrading the model at
the same endpoint does not.

When it updates, Orientation sends the stored text of up to 36 of the newest
unread stories. That reveals which of those stories are unread. It does not
send the rest of your Library, your reading history, Reader Memory, or
credentials. An Ollama server on the same machine counts as part of your
installation; any other endpoint is external. If Rill can't determine the
endpoint for a provider, set `RILL_AGENT_BASE_URL`.

Rill checks every quoted passage against the text it supplied and returns
mismatches to the agent to correct. An update gets 4 model requests, 8 tool
calls, 64,000 tokens, US$0.50, and two minutes. If you ask a question while
Orientation is updating, Rill stops the update and answers your question
first.

When an update fails, Orientation shows the error message, and
**Error details** shows the full condition and backtrace. These details stay in
your browser session; Rill does not store them or send them to telemetry.

## Rating answers

You can rate an Orientation or an Ask Rill answer as helpful or not, with
optional reasons and a comment. Ratings are private to the Reader and keep a
copy of the rated answer. **My saved ratings** lets you review, change,
withdraw, or download them.

With the Reader's permission, an operator can read them with
`list_reader_feedback()`. `reader_feedback_samples()` and
`evaluate_reader_feedback()` turn ratings into a
[vitals](https://vitals.tidyverse.org) evaluation for comparing prompt or
model changes.

## Reader Memory pilot

Set `RILL_READER_MEMORY_ENABLED=true` to try Reader Memory. It lets you save
preferences, and interpretations tied to an exact passage from a story, for
Ask Rill to consult later. Nothing is saved until you choose
**Accept as Reader Memory**; typing, reviewing, and chatting don't save
anything. You can inspect, correct, archive, and restore saved memories.
Archiving keeps the record but stops Ask Rill from using it. Accepted memories,
including their passages, are sent to the provider when Ask Rill consults
them.

The pilot is off by default because it can't permanently delete a memory yet
([Graft #48](https://github.com/JamesHWade/graft/issues/48)). Memories are
stored with [graft](https://github.com/JamesHWade/graft) in PostgreSQL. In
the demo they last until R restarts.
